descriptionChirho: The shades or ghosts of the dead dwelling in Sheol, the shadowy denizens of the underworld. Used in wisdom literature of those who descend to death (Prov 2:18 'the departed spirits', Prov 9:18, Prov 21:16), in prophetic texts of the dead being roused at the king of Babylon's descent to Sheol (Isa 14:9 'shades'), in Isaiah's resurrection oracle (Isa 26:14, 26:19 'the shades'), and in Psalms of the dead in Sheol (Ps 88:10 'the departed spirits'). Job 26:5 uses the form with the article (ha-repha'im) for the shades trembling beneath the waters. Cross-linguistically: arb consistently al-arwah ('the spirits'), deu 'Totengeister' ('spirits of the dead'), fra 'ombres' ('shadows'), hin 'mritak' ('the deceased'), kor 'jeugeun jadeul' ('the dead ones'), spa 'los muertos/sombras'. All represent the same core concept of the powerless dead in the netherworld, distinct from the ethnic group Rephaim (H7497).
